title: Non-resident pharmacy reporting under 247 CMR 20.00
rule_summary: The reporting requirements in 247 CMR 20.02 do not apply to non-resident pharmacies. A non-resident pharmacy, non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy and non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy shall comply with all provisions of 247 CMR 20.00 unless otherwise provided. A non-resident pharmacy shall report to the Board any improper dispensing, into Massachusetts, of a prescription drug that results in serious injury or death within seven business days of discovery of the improper dispensing.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate checks which pharmacy is in front of them before applying 247 CMR 20.02, since the non-resident duty starts its seven business days from discovery of the improper dispensing rather than from discovery of the serious injury or death.

authority.name: Duty to report certain improper drug dispensing and serious adverse drug events to the Board

numeric_facts.fact: non-resident pharmacy report of improper dispensing into Massachusetts resulting in serious injury or death
numeric_facts.conditions: of discovery of the improper dispensing

common_confusions: 247 CMR 20.02 is switched off for a non-resident pharmacy, but the rest of 247 CMR 20.00 still applies unless otherwise provided.
The two seven-business-day periods start from different events.
verification_notes: Read in the official 247 CMR 20.02(5) and 247 CMR 20.07 text published at mass.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
